title: Sports roundup: FKF signs KSh54m Red Cross deal, Liverpool win in Bruges, Bayern and PSG stumble
key_points: FKF and the Kenya Red Cross signed a KSh54 million deal for ambulances and first aid at league matches.
Tusker beat Posta Rangers 2-1 in the FKF Premier League; Nairobi City Thunder lost at home in the Road to BAL.
Liverpool won 3-0 at Club Brugge; Manchester United drew 2-2 at Sporting.
Lille beat Bayern Munich 2-1 and Roma ended PSG's perfect Champions League run with a 2-2 draw.
content:
Here is the top sports news of the last two days, starting at home.

FKF and Red Cross sign KSh54m medical deal

The Football Kenya Federation (FKF) and the Kenya Red Cross Society signed a KSh54 million partnership in Nairobi on Tuesday, November 24, Citizen Digital and other outlets reported. The deal provides ambulances, first aid, training for medical staff and equipment such as stretchers at matches in the FKF Premier League, the Women's Premier League, the National Super League and the Women's National Super League, plus international games. Division One gets first aid.

FKF president Hussein Mohammed also challenged the national team to reach the 2030 World Cup. "Kenya must qualify for World Cup 2030," he said, according to Citizen Digital. Kenya has never played at a World Cup finals.

FKF Premier League: Tusker beat Posta Rangers

Tusker beat Posta Rangers 2-1 on Wednesday at St Sebastian Park in Murang'a, Mozzart Sport and 365Scores reported. Chrisphine Erambo and Victor Mbaoma scored for Tusker before Mark Shaban pulled one back late for Posta. Mozzart Sport says it was Tusker's third win of the season.

In other games reported by Mozzart Sport, 10-man APS Bomet drew 0-0 with Migori Youth, and Nairobi United beat 3K FC 2-0.

Basketball: Thunder lose at home

Kenyan champions Nairobi City Thunder lost 83-71 to Zambia's Munali Suns at Kasarani on Tuesday in the Road to BAL Elite 16, Capital FM and Citizen Digital reported. The score was 37-37 at half-time before the Suns pulled away. Tylor Ongwae led Thunder with 21 points. Thunder face South Sudan's Patriots BC on Thursday night.

Champions League: Liverpool cruise, United held

In Wednesday's Champions League games:

  • Club Brugge 0-3 Liverpool: Alexander Isak scored twice and Florian Wirtz once. Liverpool now have 12 points from five games.
  • Sporting 2-2 Manchester United: Bruno Fernandes scored twice soon after half-time, once from the penalty spot, but Sporting's Luis Suarez also scored twice. United's Youri Tielemans was sent off late. New coach Mauricio Pochettino is still waiting for his first win.
  • Lille 2-1 Bayern Munich: Dayot Upamecano put Bayern ahead, but Ayase Ueda and an own goal turned it around. It was Bayern's first defeat of the season.
  • PSG 2-2 Roma: A late Donyell Malen penalty ended PSG's run of four wins from four in the league phase.
  • Sabah 1-4 Barcelona: Anthony Gordon scored twice.
  • Also: Inter 2-0 Stuttgart, Atletico Madrid 2-0 Viking, Shakhtar 0-1 Fenerbahce, Slavia Prague 0-1 Villarreal.

Ivory Coast winger Amad Diallo had a goal ruled out for Manchester United in Lisbon.

Coming up

Kenya's sevens team, Shujaa, plays at the Dubai tournament from November 27 to 29, according to Citizen Digital. The CAF Champions League group stage also starts this weekend.
